title: The button-at-L18 subspace family on the HELD-OUT VALIDATION split: the one cell of the dissociation that has never been run, at the family size that certifies, with a LIVE rejection region for the first time on the button side

opened_by_instruction: Write and freeze the preregistration for the button L18 VALIDATION subspace family. It has never been run.
question: PR-CSI-005 (S-137) measured button's rank-1 installation axis at L18 against 46 norm-matched controls on TRAIN and found it ranks 36 of 47 (rank p 0.766, attainable floor 0.0213, candidate recovery -0.00014 against a whole-state +0.10938). That is a CERTIFIED failure rather than a floor-limited one: at K = 46 the floor is 0.0213, so 'DOES NOT PASS' is a result and not an artifact of family size. But it is TRAIN ONLY. Basket's axis passes at L18 on BOTH splits (rank 1 of 47 train, rank 1 of 47 validation). The dissociation is therefore currently asymmetric in its evidence: two splits on the passing side, one split on the failing side, and the dissociation analysis's own section 13 holds that held-out is the strongest evidence in the set. THE QUESTION: does button's L18 failure REPLICATE on the 23 held-out validation domains, at the same family size, the same procedure, and the same layer?
hypothesis: H1 (what is actually being tested, and it is the prediction the sprint's own committed result implies): button's rank-1 axis at L18 does NOT rescue installation on held-out domains either, and ranks in the upper half of its 46 norm-matched controls. H0 (the null the rank test is against): cand_rank1 is exchangeable with its 46 norm-matched control directions with respect to y_install recovery (KO_X - KO), domain-clustered, so its rank among itself and the 46 is uniform on {1..47} and p = rank/47. NOTE THE DIRECTION OF THE ASYMMETRY, which is the opposite of PR-CSI-005's: here a REJECTION of H0 would CONTRADICT the sprint's committed headline. This experiment can hurt the dissociation and cannot help it.
why_this_is_a_LIVE_test_and_PR_CSI_005_w: PR-CSI-005 pooled 10 already-read controls with 36 new ones. Seven of the 10 already beat the candidate, so R47 >= 8 was ARITHMETIC before a single new arm ran and the rejection region {R47 <= 2} was UNREACHABLE. Its primary therefore had to be X, the exceedance count among the blind 36, and its pooled rank was explicitly a measurement rather than a test. THIS FAMILY IS ENTIRELY NEW. Not one of its 54 arms exists. There are no committed exceedances, there is no arithmetic floor, and every one of the 47 ranks is attainable. The POOLED RANK IS THE PRIMARY here and it is a real test with attainable p floor 1/47 = 0.021277 and a live rejection region. That is a design improvement over PR-CSI-005 and it is bought entirely by the family being new.
what_is_actually_at_stake: (a) Whether S-137's sentence 'button's failure is CERTIFIED rather than floor-limited' is a property of the TRAIN split or of button's axis. (b) Whether the codeword dissociation is a two-split result on both sides or a two-split/one-split result, which is what the dissociation analysis's section 13 ranking of evidence turns on. (c) Whether the direction-A axis swap (PR-CSI-006, S-138, corrected in REVIEW R10) can ever be read held-out: direction A -- basket's axis into button's knockout, rank 4 of 47 on TRAIN -- has no validation reading and cannot have one until a button L18 validation control family of 46 exists. This preregistration builds exactly that family, and the swap arm is declared here as a SECONDARY, never as the primary.

THE_BASE_KO_REUSE_QUESTION_ARGUED_EXPLIC.the_case_FOR_reuse: BASE and KO run no rescue at all. Launcher lines 155-156 pass them neither $R nor --rescue-basis, so their computation has no layer parameter and their RUNMETA records args.rescue_layer == null. the_case_AGAINST_reuse_and_it_wins_on_th: (1) BLOB. They ran under blob 73e541f1, +527/-7 lines from the blob this family will run under, with git_dirty == true so the executed bytes are unrecoverable. KO is not an incidental arm: it is the SUBTRAHEND of every single recovery in the family (recovery = arm - KO, for the candidate and for all 46 controls alike). Admitting a KO from a different, unrecoverable blob puts an unverifiable term into all 47 numbers at once. S-142 refused to launch 8.7 GPU-hours over exactly this hazard in a case where the drift was +17 lines; here it is +527/-7 and dirty.

(2) KEY INTERSECTION. The analyser reduces every admitted arm on ONE cross-arm common key set. A BASE/KO pair produced by different code can shift which prompt keys survive the option-mass gate, and that shift would propagate into all 47 recoveries through the shared intersection rather than into two arms.

(3) THE LAYER FILTER CANNOT PROTECT THE READ. Because BASE and KO carry rescue_layer == null in BOTH their L18 and L20 copies, --require-rescue-layer 18 passes both silently. If the L20 copies were admitted they would be admitted INVISIBLY. The only separator is --require-slurm-job, which is exactly the S-104 / S-127 / R8-B1 foot-gun. Re-running BASE and KO under the new jobs removes the ambiguity at its source instead of relying on a filter to catch it.

bootstrap_and_permutation_procedure.bootstrap: domain-clustered nonparametric bootstrap, the analyser's default --n-boot 20000, resampling the 23 VALIDATION domains with replacement and recomputing the contrast within each draw. Used for the CIs on contrasts, NOT for the rank.
bootstrap_and_permutation_procedure.permutation: the rank itself IS the permutation test: under exchangeability of the candidate with its K controls the rank is uniform on {1..K+1} and p = rank/(K+1). No additional resampling is performed on it and none may be added afterwards.

bootstrap_and_permutation_procedure.seeds: the analyser's own; no seed is chosen here, and re-running with a different seed to obtain a different number is prohibited by name.
bootstrap_and_permutation_procedure.n_is_23_not_230: every resample is over 23 DOMAINS. The 230 rows are not the unit and may never be resampled as if they were.

prediction_fixed_before_data.why_a_band_from_two_routes_and_not_one_n: The only calibrating data is button's own TRAIN L18 46-control read. Carrying its exceedance RATE forward unchanged ignores that validation has 23 domains instead of 67 and is therefore noisier; correcting for that noise shrinks the effect toward the uniform-null centre of 24. Both are defensible, they differ by about 6 ranks, and freezing only the one that flatters the sprint's committed conclusion would be the move REVIEW R10's BLOCKER-1 was written about. Both are frozen.

ROUTE_1_Jeffreys_Beta_binomial_the_metho.method: Jeffreys Beta(0.5, 0.5) prior on the per-control exceedance probability, updated on button's MEASURED TRAIN L18 count of 35 exceedances among 46 controls, giving Beta(35.5, 11.5) with posterior mean 0.755319. Then X_val ~ BetaBinomial(46, 35.5, 11.5) and R47 = 1 + X.
ROUTE_1_Jeffreys_Beta_binomial_the_metho.numbers: E[X] = 34.7447, sd = 4.0585, median 35; 2.5% quantile 26, 97.5% quantile 42. Hence E[R47] = 35.74, 95% predictive R47 in [27, 43].
ROUTE_1_Jeffreys_Beta_binomial_the_metho.the_honest_weakness_of_this_route: It treats the 46 validation draws as exchangeable with the 46 train draws at the same exceedance probability, which ignores the split's 2.9-fold smaller domain count entirely. Its tails are consequently far too thin and I do not use them as the operative thresholds.

ROUTE_2_normal_z_with_split_noise_shrink.method: Compute the family-size-free z on TRAIN, shrink it by the ratio of the two splits' domain-clustered standard errors, and read the implied exceedance probability off a normal control family.
ROUTE_2_normal_z_with_split_noise_shrink.step_1_z_on_train: MEASURED from the 46 recovery values in reports/DCS_CSI_SUBSPACE_button_train_L18_n46.json: control mean +0.000283696, control sd 0.00074304, candidate -0.00014, so z_train = (-0.00014 - 0.000283696)/0.00074304 = -0.5702.
ROUTE_2_normal_z_with_split_noise_shrink.step_2_the_shrinkage_and_its_justificati: The recovery of each arm is a mean over domain means, so its standard error scales as 1/sqrt(n_domains). Validation has 23 domains against train's 67, so every arm's noise inflates by sqrt(67/23) = 1.7067. The candidate's SYSTEMATIC offset from its control family does not change with the split, but sd(controls) -- the denominator of z -- is itself driven by that per-arm noise and inflates by the same factor. Hence z_val = z_train * sqrt(23/67) = -0.5702 * 0.5859 = -0.3341. This shrinks the candidate toward the middle of its family, i.e. toward rank 24.
ROUTE_2_normal_z_with_split_noise_shrink.step_3_the_implied_rank: p_exceed = 1 - Phi(-0.3341) = 0.63085, so E[R47] = 1 + 46*0.63085 = 30.02, with binomial sd sqrt(46*p*(1-p)) = 3.273, giving R47 roughly [24, 37] at +/- 2 sd.
ROUTE_2_normal_z_with_split_noise_shrink.the_honest_weakness_of_this_route: It assumes the control family is approximately normal and that the candidate's offset is entirely systematic. If part of the train offset was itself noise, the true shrinkage is stronger and the prediction should sit even closer to 24.

MDE_and_power.on_the_PRIMARY: A rank test has no continuous MDE. Its attainable outcomes are the 47 ranks; the smallest attainable p is 0.021277 and it requires the candidate to strictly exceed ALL 46 controls. THE INSTRUMENT DEMONSTRABLY RESOLVES THAT AT THIS SAMPLE SIZE: basket's native axis achieved rank 1 of 47 on THIS EXACT SPLIT -- 23 domains, 46 controls, L18, same procedure -- with recovery +0.00401 and 0/46 exceedances (reports/DCS_CSI_SUBSPACE_basket_validation_n46.json, VERDICT PRIMARY PASSES). That is the only power statement this design supports and I am not manufacturing a second one.
MDE_and_power.what_the_23_domains_cost: Every arm's domain-clustered standard error is sqrt(67/23) = 1.71x its train counterpart. A candidate that sits z = -0.57 inside its train family sits z = -0.33 inside its validation family under the noise model of route 2, so the design's ability to distinguish 'clearly inside the family' from 'at the boundary' is materially weaker than on train. It is NOT weaker at detecting a PASS: a pass requires exceeding all 46 controls, and basket did exactly that here.
MDE_and_power.what_would_be_needed_to_give_button_a_re: A candidate recovery exceeding the maximum of its 46 norm-matched controls. On TRAIN at L18 that maximum is +0.00179 against a candidate of -0.00014, about 2.6 control-sd short. On validation the control family will be wider, so the bar in absolute terms is higher, not lower. No family size and no split fixes that, and this preregistration is not run in the hope that it does.
MDE_and_power.on_the_family_size_free_z: With 46 controls, sd(controls) is estimated to within roughly 1/sqrt(2*45) ~ 10.5%, so S1 is a tight comparison against button TRAIN's -0.5702 and against basket's validation value.

decision_rule.step_5: Report S1 (z), S2 (exceedance rate with Clopper-Pearson CI), S3 (subfamily ranks), S4 (leave-one-domain-out histogram), S5 (specificity_holm) and S6 (candidate minus comparator). success_criterion: The held-out cell is ASSIGNED: all gates pass, the size assertions print 46 controls and 23 domains, R47 is read once, and the branch of decision_rule.on_R47 that R47 selects is reported with its prespecified text. 'Success' means the experiment ANSWERED, not that any particular branch came up. R47 >= 24 is a success. R47 <= 2 is a success. The design succeeds and the sprint's headline loses.
failure_criterion: The design fails, as a design, if the cell cannot be assigned: if any required gate fails, if the family cannot reach 46 controls, if n_domains is not 23, if a VOID condition fires, or if any rank is reported without its asserted denominator. FAILURE OF THE DESIGN IS NOT A NULL RESULT AND MUST NEVER BE REPORTED AS ONE. 'CANNOT ANSWER' is not 'DOES NOT PASS'.
what_this_experiment_does_NOT_settle: It cannot explain WHY the codewords differ. It can only say whether button's L18 failure replicates held-out. The residual after eight killed or partial candidate explanations is still the codeword and it is still unexplained.

It cannot make button pass in any sense that would license 'button's axis is causal'. Prohibition 19 stands. On TRAIN the candidate recovers -0.13% of what the whole clean state recovers; no rank at any family size enlarges an effect.

It says nothing about button at its OWN layer L20 at matched family size. configs/dcs_csi_axis_button_behavioral.pt carries only 8 random + 5 shuffled rank-1 controls, so an L20 family of 46 would need 33 new bases built first. The existing L20 validation read is K = 10, floor 0.0909, and certifies nothing.
It says nothing about the NECESSITY direction (--rescue-donor ko), which is PR-CSI-003/003A and which S-142 left blocked on the blob question.

It does not test candidate C1 ('basket's probe is simply a better probe'). The direction-A swap arm is a declared SECONDARY here and, whatever it returns, REVIEW R10's BLOCKER-1 governs what may be said about C1.

It cannot separate the split from the blob for POINT VALUES compared against PR-CSI-005's train family. The domains are disjoint and the blobs differ; see THE_BLOB_QUESTION.WHAT_THIS_DOES_AND_DOES_NOT_LET_ME_COMPARE_AGAINST_PR_CSI_005.
It cannot generalise beyond rank 1. cand_rank1 is the rank-1 row; button's selected_rank is 5 and KO_PLS (cand_pls5) is reported but is not the candidate.

With 23 domains it is a materially noisier read than the train cell, and it cannot distinguish 'clearly inside the family' from 'at the boundary' as sharply. That is declared in MDE_and_power and is not a caveat to be discovered afterwards.
must_not_be_said_if_positive: NOT 'button's axis is causal' or 'button's axis works'. Prohibition 19 stands in every branch. A rank cannot enlarge an effect, and on train the effect is -0.13% of the whole-state recovery.
NOT 'the dissociation is refuted' on anything short of R47 <= 2. R47 <= 12 is the top quartile and does NOT certify (p >= 0.0638); it is a replication failure, not a pass.
NOT 'nearly significant' about any R47 >= 3. p = R47/47 and the nearest certifying value is 2. There is nothing to be near.

NOT any claim at all if the size assertion in decision_rule step_2 was not printed. A rank without its denominator is the S-134 vacuous gate wearing a result's clothes, and REVIEW R10's BLOCKER-2 is the fourth instance of exactly that.
NOT 'this replicates the train result in reverse' or any statement pooling this family's controls with the train family's. The domains are disjoint and the blobs differ.
NOT 'basket's axis rescues button held-out' from the SECONDARY, under any outcome. If the secondary returns R47 <= 2 the splits disagree and PR-CSI-006 step_6 yields NOT REPLICATED and NO CELL.
NOT any statement pooling button and basket, and NOT any statement that a result on one transfers to the other (rule 3.3).

NOT a restatement of S-138's withdrawn headline ('C1 SUPPORTED and the STATE hypothesis REFUTED') in any form, in any branch, in the body or in a title. REVIEW R10's BLOCKER-1 is binding and the failure it records was a title that moved a cell the body had assigned correctly.
must_not_be_said_if_null: NOT 'the dissociation is now proven'. A rank of 32 of 47 for button is the ABSENCE of an effect for button; it is not a positive result and it certifies nothing about basket. Basket's 1 of 47 is the only certified cell and it remains the only one.
NOT 'button's axis is not causal'. Prohibition 19 cuts both ways. This measures rescue under one knockout at one layer on one readout.
NOT 'replicated' without naming what replicated: a VERDICT (does not pass) on disjoint domains under a different score_behavior.py blob. The ranks are comparable; the point values are not compared.
NOT 'the codewords differ because ...'. This experiment supplies no mechanism.

NOT 'underpowered'. With K = 46 the floor is 0.021277 and basket's native axis attained rank 1 of 47 on THIS split with THESE 23 domains. The instrument resolved a real effect here and a null is a null.
NOT any suggestion that more controls, a different layer, a different rank or the other split would have changed the answer, unless that experiment is separately preregistered and run.
NOT 'the TRAIN own-layer headline is now supported'. This is the SHARED layer L18 on HELD-OUT domains and it does not speak to the L20 own-layer cell, whose delta-z CI includes zero.
NOT 'C3 is closed' or any statement about the unequal-control-family explanation. That was PR-CSI-005's subject and it is not reopened or closed here.
